label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Hey Mikaela, sorry it's taken me a few days to get back to you. Happy to give you the real version, you lot were bloody good to us when Dave did his shoulder so I owe you a straight answer. Good and bad.

Bit of background first. We're 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept, once mating had kicked off. We skip Tues, Thurs and Sat arvos plus Sunday arvo, so that's 4 once-a-days a week. Mornings are 5.15 every day.

Production: going off the Fonterra app we're about 6% down on the same weeks last year. Our rep had told us to expect 8-10%, so it's been better than he said. It's still a hit though, I'm not going to pretend otherwise. You'll want to do your own sums on what 6% looks like for you.

Cells: yes they jumped. We went from about 110k to around 180k in the first 3 weeks, which gave me a fright. They've come back to about 135k now, so better, but still higher than we were.

The worst bit: we had a heifer get mastitis and it went bad on a skipped arvo. We didn't spot her till the next morning and she lost a quarter. That one's on us, but it's the kind of thing that happens when you're not seeing them twice a day. You really have to be on your game with teat spraying, and with actually walking through and checking the cows on the skip days. If you get slack it bites you. I'd say that's the biggest thing to get right if you go for it.

The cows came round quicker than I expected. We had about 4 days of them bellowing at the gate in the arvo and then they were fine.

Now the good stuff. Lameness is way down. There are 4 on the lame list now, and this time last year we had 11. Our walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km so that's made a real difference.

The people side has been the biggest thing for us though. Kieran, our 2IC, told me it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. Sounds like that's exactly where your young fella's at, so I'd take that seriously. And on the first skipped Sunday arvo Dave and I drove over to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20 odd years. I nearly cried in the car lol.

With Tom's knees, honestly I think the arvos off will help him more than anything else would. Fewer trips to the shed, less walking up and down the pit, a bit of a breather in the middle of the week.

For me, I wouldn't go back. The hours alone are worth the 6%. But I don't want to sell it to you and then have you cursing me in March if it doesn't suit your farm. It does take more watching than you'd think, especially at the start, and your cells probably will go up for a bit. If your vet's on board, that's a good sign. Get them to keep an eye on things with you for the first month or so.

Come and have a look at our shed rosters and the numbers at the field day on the 19th. I'll bring them along and you can go through them properly. Same goes for you Grant if you're still keen.

Or just ring me, much easier than texting, my thumbs are useless on this thing. Any time.

Bev
